title: Closures (beginner-to-intermediate)
learningObjectives: Explain closures (beginner-to-intermediate) and use functions with clear scope and behaviour.

understand.concept: A closure is formed when a function retains access to bindings from its lexical environment after the outer function has finished executing. Closures are used for private state, callbacks, and function factories.
understand.whyItMatters: Closures explain how callbacks can remember values and how modules can encapsulate state. They can also retain memory longer than expected if references remain reachable.
understand.analogy: A closure is like a function carrying access to the surrounding environment it was created in.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; function execution, scope, closures, and call stacks follow JavaScript runtime rules.

explain.narrative: The returned function retains access to count, so each call increments the same private variable.

examples.explanation: The returned function retains access to count, so each call increments the same private variable.
examples.expectedOutput: The browser console displays the function results described.

practise.guidedTask: Create a function factory that returns a function with private state. Explain which outer binding the returned function remembers.
practise.independentTask: Build a small reusable function example. Test inputs, scope boundaries, and any retained state or side effects.
hints: Keep functions focused and names descriptive.
Know whether a callback is synchronous or asynchronous.
Add a base case to every recursive function.

practice.starterCode:
<!doctype html>
<html lang="en"><head><meta charset="utf-8"><meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1"><title>Closures (beginner-to-intermediate)</title></head><body>
<script>function makeCounter(){let count=0;return function(){count++;return count;};}const next=makeCounter();console.log(next(),next(),next());</script>
</body></html>

questions.prompt: What does a closure retain access to?
questions.explanation: A closure retains access to the lexical environment in which the function was created.

questions.prompt: What makes a function easier to reason about?
options: Clear inputs, limited responsibilities, and known side effects
questions.answer: Clear inputs, limited responsibilities, and known side effects
questions.explanation: Explicit dependencies and controlled side effects improve clarity and testability.
